messages:
sofia: FYI customer CS-4821 reporting streaming responses stall ~30s after idle, then buffer drops entire message. WSS over Private VPC. They say it looks like middlebox buffering.
keith: Can you paste a short repro and the endpoint they hit?
sofia: Repro steps from customer: `wscat -c \"wss://private.redwood.example.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-xx\"` then send a prompt, responses stream fine for a minute, then no more data until connection closes and client receives chunked payload all at once.
matt: Sounds like a corporate proxy doing TLS rewrap or buffering frames. Any TLS errors in our logs?
sofia: No TLS handshake failures on our side. Connection stays ESTABLISHED. Last log shows no data for ~35s then connection reset by peer.
keith: Ask for a tcpdump from their edge (before their proxy) and from our side (Customer IP). Also check if their egress allowlist is routing through a middlebox.
sofia: I asked them to run:
```
# on customer edge
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host api.redwood.example.com and tcp port 443 -w cs4821-client.pcap
# on our compute (they provided VPC flow logs)
```
sofia: Customer returned pcap — I can see TLS records for a while, then a burst of smaller TLS records from the proxy, then long silence, then RST.
matt: Small TLS records + silence = application layer buffering or DPI reassembly. Could be their proxy buffering until full HTTP/2 DATA frames available. Are we using HTTP/1.1 upgrade or raw websocket frames?
sofia: This private endpoint is behind TLS + ALB terminating TLS -> internal Nginx reverse proxy -> runtime. We do an HTTP/1.1 Upgrade to websocket.
keith: If the edge proxy rewrites TLS (TLS rewrap) it might inject its own idle timeouts. Ask customer to check corporate proxy idle timeout or transparent TLS interception appliance.
sofia: I asked customer to check firewall/proxy logs. They found a Palo Alto inline decryption policy with 30s TCP idle timeout, which will buffer until it sees a full packet or timeout.
infra-bot: Deploy metrics: no spikes on our egress or runtime. Keepalive pings from client aren't received after middlebox.
keith: Two actionable fixes: 1) Request customer add our host to their egress allowlist so traffic bypasses the TLS intercepting proxy (preferred). 2) As mitigation, enable websocket-level heartbeats/pings every 15s from client to keep middlebox from idling.
sofia: Customer tried adding `--ping-interval 10` in their client lib, still saw buffering unless they bypassed proxy.
matt: That suggests proxy is buffering entire HTTP payloads ignoring websocket pings (some DPI devices don't forward small frames). If they can, try bypassing DPI for our endpoint.
sofia: They modified their firewall to allow direct egress to our public IPs and the issue stopped. Streaming resumed without chunked dumps.
keith: Good. For Private customers we should document this: require egress to avoid TLS-rewrapping middleboxes, or ensure midbox supports per-frame forwarding and >120s idle.
sofia: Filing KB draft: "Websockets and middleboxes (TLS rewrap/DPI) — symptoms, tcpdump hints, customer mitigations (egress allowlist, client pings)". Assigning to @matt to review.
matt: Will review. Also suggest we add runtime logs to detect long silent intervals and surface a support hint automatically.
sre_oncall: For immediate support, we can add a quick diagnostic command customers can run: `openssl s_client -connect host:443 -servername host -quiet` then `> GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1` to inspect behavior, and `tshark -r` for small TLS record patterns.
sofia: Customer agreed to update their network docs and reach out to infra team to whitelist our FQDNs. Closing for now but leaving note to follow up in 3 days to confirm no recurrence. :white_check_mark:
keith: Nice triage. Add the pcap excerpts to CS-4821 before closing.
sofia: Done. Attaching pcap snippet and summary in the support ticket.
